description: An introduction to elements, compounds and mixtures, chemical symbols, fixed and variable composition, and the physical methods used to separate mixtures such as filtration, distillation and magnetic separation.

mcq.questionText: An element is a pure substance that:

options.text: Can be broken down into simpler substances
Cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means

mcq.explanation: An element is made of only one kind of atom and cannot be split into simpler substances chemically. Exam Tip: Elements are the building blocks (oxygen, iron, gold). Compounds CAN be broken down; elements cannot.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an element?
mcq.explanation: Water and salt are compounds; air is a mixture; oxygen is a single element. Exam Tip: Water (H2O) and salt (NaCl) are compounds; air is a mixture. Only oxygen is an element.

mcq.questionText: The chemical symbol for the element oxygen is:
mcq.explanation: Oxygen is represented by the single capital letter O. Exam Tip: One-letter symbols are a single CAPITAL (O, H, N, C). Two-letter symbols are capital + small (Na, Cl, Mg).

mcq.questionText: The chemical symbol for sodium is:
mcq.explanation: Sodium's Latin name natrium gives Na. Exam Tip: Latin-based symbols: sodium Na, potassium K, iron Fe, lead Pb.

mcq.questionText: A compound is a pure substance formed when two or more elements combine:

options.text: Physically and can be separated easily

mcq.explanation: The elements join chemically in a fixed (definite) ratio. Exam Tip: Compound = elements chemically combined in a FIXED ratio (water is always H2O, 2 H to 1 O).

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a compound?
mcq.explanation: Water is hydrogen and oxygen chemically combined (H2O). Exam Tip: Iron, oxygen and copper are elements. Water is a compound.

mcq.questionText: A mixture differs from a compound because a mixture:

options.text: Can be separated by physical methods
Is formed by a chemical reaction

mcq.explanation: In a mixture the substances are not chemically joined; they can be separated physically. Exam Tip: Mixture = physically combined, variable composition, separated physically. Compound = chemically combined, fixed, separated chemically.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a mixture?
mcq.explanation: Air is a mixture of gases (nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide and others). Exam Tip: Air's composition varies and its gases keep their properties, so it is a mixture.

mcq.questionText: The method used to separate an insoluble solid from a liquid is:
mcq.explanation: The solid is trapped by filter paper while the liquid passes through, which is filtration. Exam Tip: Filtration separates an insoluble solid (sand) from a liquid. Solid = residue; liquid = filtrate.

mcq.questionText: Which method is used to obtain pure water from salty water?
mcq.explanation: Distillation boils the water to vapour, then condenses it, leaving the salt behind. Exam Tip: Distillation recovers the SOLVENT (pure water). Simple evaporation would give the salt but lose the water.

mcq.questionText: The best method to separate iron filings from a mixture of iron filings and sulphur powder is:
mcq.explanation: Iron is magnetic; sulphur is not. A magnet attracts and removes the iron filings only. Exam Tip: Magnetic separation works when ONE component is magnetic (iron, cobalt, nickel).

mcq.questionText: To obtain salt from a solution of salt in water, the suitable method is:
mcq.explanation: Evaporating the water leaves the solid salt behind. Exam Tip: To recover a DISSOLVED SOLID, evaporate the water. To recover the WATER, use distillation.

mcq.questionText: When common salt (a compound) is compared with its elements sodium and chlorine, which statement is TRUE?

options.text: Salt has the same properties as sodium and chlorine
Salt has completely different properties from sodium and chlorine
Salt is a mixture of sodium and chlorine
Salt can be separated by filtration

mcq.explanation: Sodium is a reactive metal and chlorine a poisonous gas, yet their compound (salt) is a safe, edible solid. Exam Tip: A compound has NEW properties, different from its elements. This is a key difference from a mixture.

mcq.questionText: The method used to separate two miscible liquids with different boiling points, such as ethanol and water, is:
mcq.explanation: Fractional distillation separates them using the difference in boiling points. Exam Tip: Ethanol (b.p. 78 C) comes off before water (b.p. 100 C).

mcq.questionText: A mixture of oil and water can be separated using a:
mcq.explanation: Oil and water are immiscible and form separate layers; a separating funnel runs off the lower layer first. Exam Tip: Immiscible liquids (oil/water) use a separating funnel. The denser liquid settles below.

fib.questionText: A pure substance made of only one type of atom is called an ____.
fib.explanation: A substance with only one type of atom is an element, which cannot be broken down chemically. Exam Tip: Elements cannot be broken down chemically, for example gold, oxygen and iron.

fib.questionText: The chemical symbol for iron is ____.
fib.explanation: Iron's symbol Fe comes from its Latin name ferrum. Exam Tip: From the Latin ferrum. Latin symbols: iron Fe, sodium Na, potassium K, lead Pb, copper Cu.

fib.questionText: A substance formed when two or more elements combine chemically in a fixed ratio is a ____.
fib.explanation: Elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio form a compound. Exam Tip: Compound = fixed composition, new properties, separated only chemically.

fib.questionText: A ____ is formed when substances are mixed physically and can be separated by physical methods.
fib.explanation: Substances mixed physically and separable by physical means form a mixture. Exam Tip: Air, soil and sea water are mixtures with variable composition, and their components keep their properties.

fib.questionText: The method of separating an insoluble solid from a liquid using filter paper is called ____.
fib.explanation: Using filter paper to hold back an insoluble solid from a liquid is filtration. Exam Tip: Filtration gives a residue (solid) and a filtrate (liquid).

fib.questionText: The process of obtaining a pure liquid from a solution by boiling and then condensing the vapour is called ____.
fib.explanation: Boiling a solution and condensing the vapour to collect a pure liquid is distillation. Exam Tip: Distillation recovers the solvent, such as pure water from a salt solution.

fib.questionText: The symbol for the element hydrogen is ____.
fib.explanation: Hydrogen is represented by the single capital letter H. Exam Tip: Single-letter symbols use one CAPITAL: H, O, N, C.

fib.questionText: In a compound, the elements are present in a ____ ratio by mass.
fib.explanation: The elements in a compound combine in a fixed, definite ratio by mass. Exam Tip: Water is always 2 hydrogen to 1 oxygen, and this fixed ratio never changes.

fib.questionText: The separation method that uses a magnet to remove a magnetic substance from a mixture is called ____ separation.
fib.explanation: Using a magnet to pull out a magnetic component is magnetic separation. Exam Tip: Works only if one component is magnetic (iron, cobalt, nickel).

fib.questionText: In filtration, the clear liquid that passes through the filter paper is called the ____.
fib.explanation: The liquid that passes through the filter paper is the filtrate. Exam Tip: Filtrate = liquid through; residue = solid left on the paper.

tf.questionText: An element cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.
tf.explanation: Elements are the chemical building blocks and cannot be split chemically. Exam Tip: Only compounds can be broken down chemically.
Water is not an element because it is made of two elements joined together. Exam Tip: Water (H2O) is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.

tf.questionText: In a mixture, the substances keep their own properties.
tf.explanation: Because they are only physically combined, the substances in a mixture keep their properties. Exam Tip: Mixtures keep properties; compounds gain NEW properties.

tf.questionText: A compound can be separated into its elements by physical methods such as filtration.
tf.explanation: A compound is chemically joined, so physical methods cannot separate it. Exam Tip: Physical methods separate MIXTURES. Compounds need chemical means, for example electrolysis of water.

tf.questionText: The symbol for sodium is Na.
tf.explanation: Sodium's symbol Na comes from its Latin name. Exam Tip: From the Latin natrium.

tf.questionText: Distillation is used to obtain pure water from sea water.
tf.explanation: Distillation boils and condenses the water, leaving the dissolved salts behind. Exam Tip: Distillation recovers the pure liquid; evaporation would recover the solid.
Air is not chemically joined; its gases are only mixed together. Exam Tip: Air is the classic example of a mixture of gases.

tf.questionText: A mixture has a fixed composition by mass.
tf.explanation: A mixture has a composition that can change, so it is not fixed. Exam Tip: Fixed composition = compound; variable composition = mixture.

tf.questionText: Iron filings can be separated from sulphur using a magnet.
tf.explanation: Iron is magnetic while sulphur is not, so a magnet removes the iron. Exam Tip: Magnetic separation exploits a difference in magnetic property.

tf.questionText: In a compound, the elements combine in a variable (any) ratio.
tf.explanation: Compounds always combine their elements in a fixed ratio, not a variable one. Exam Tip: Fixed ratio = compound (water is always H2O). The statement describes a mixture.

summary.correctAnswer: A pure substance made of only one kind of atom that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.
summary.explanation: Examples include oxygen, iron and gold. Exam Tip: Elements are the building blocks of all matter.

summary.correctAnswer: A pure substance formed when two or more elements combine chemically in a fixed ratio.
summary.explanation: Water (H2O) and common salt (NaCl) are compounds. Exam Tip: A compound has new properties and can only be separated by chemical means.

summary.correctAnswer: A substance made of two or more components physically combined in any ratio that can be separated by physical methods.
summary.explanation: Air, soil and sea water are mixtures. Exam Tip: The components of a mixture keep their own properties.

summary.correctAnswer: A short letter or letters used to represent an element, such as O for oxygen or Na for sodium.
summary.explanation: One-letter symbols are a capital; two-letter symbols are a capital plus a small letter. Exam Tip: Some symbols come from Latin names, such as Fe for iron.

summary.correctAnswer: The definite proportion by mass in which the elements of a compound are always combined.
summary.explanation: Water is always 2 hydrogen to 1 oxygen. Exam Tip: A fixed ratio is a feature of compounds, not mixtures.

summary.correctAnswer: A method of separating an insoluble solid from a liquid by passing the mixture through filter paper.
summary.explanation: The solid stays as residue and the liquid passes through as filtrate. Exam Tip: Use filtration to separate sand from water.

summary.correctAnswer: A method of obtaining a pure liquid from a solution by boiling it to vapour and then condensing the vapour.
summary.explanation: It recovers the solvent, such as pure water from a salt solution. Exam Tip: Distillation keeps the liquid; evaporation keeps the solid.

summary.correctAnswer: A method of separating two or more miscible liquids using the differences in their boiling points.
summary.explanation: Ethanol (b.p. 78 C) is collected before water (b.p. 100 C). Exam Tip: Use it for miscible liquids like ethanol and water.

summary.correctAnswer: A method of separating a magnetic substance from a mixture by using a magnet.
summary.explanation: A magnet attracts iron filings but not sulphur. Exam Tip: Works only when one component is magnetic, such as iron, cobalt or nickel.

summary.correctAnswer: An apparatus used to separate two immiscible liquids by running off the lower, denser layer first.
summary.explanation: Oil and water form two layers and are separated this way. Exam Tip: Use a separating funnel for immiscible liquids like oil and water.

hoq.questionText: A student is given a mixture of sand, common salt and water. What is the correct sequence of methods to obtain pure dry salt AND pure water separately?

options.text: Filter to remove sand, then distil the salt solution to obtain water and leave salt

hoq.explanation: Sand is insoluble, so it is filtered out first as the residue. The filtrate is salt solution, and distilling it boils off and condenses the water, which is collected pure, leaving the solid salt behind. Exam Tip: Remove the INSOLUBLE solid first (filtration), then deal with the dissolved solid. Use distillation (not plain evaporation) because BOTH salt AND pure water are wanted.

hoq.questionText: A table gives properties of three substances. X: made of one type of atom. Y: two elements chemically joined, cannot be separated physically, fixed composition. Z: two substances physically mixed, can be separated physically, variable composition. Identify X, Y and Z.

options.text: X = compound, Y = element, Z = mixture
X = element, Y = compound, Z = mixture
X = mixture, Y = element, Z = compound
X = element, Y = mixture, Z = compound

hoq.explanation: X is one type of atom, so it is an element. Y is chemically joined, fixed and not physically separable, so it is a compound. Z is physically mixed, variable and physically separable, so it is a mixture. Exam Tip: One atom type = element; chemically joined and fixed = compound; physically mixed and variable = mixture.

hoq.questionText: When 8 g of iron filings are mixed with 4 g of sulphur powder, the mixture can be separated with a magnet. But when the same mixture is heated strongly, it forms a new grey solid (iron sulphide) that a magnet can no longer separate. What has happened?

options.text: A mixture became a compound; the elements combined chemically, forming a new substance with new properties
Nothing changed; it is still a mixture

hoq.explanation: Before heating, iron and sulphur are simply mixed and a magnet removes the iron. On strong heating they react and combine chemically to form iron sulphide, a new non-magnetic substance, so the magnet no longer works. Exam Tip: The classic iron + sulphur experiment. Before heating = mixture; after heating = compound. Loss of magnetism is the evidence a compound formed.
